html:
Around 370 the Huns, nomads from the steppe east of the Volga, crossed into Europe and attacked the peoples north of the Black Sea. It set off the great movement of peoples that ended Roman rule in the west.

Where the Huns came from is unknown. Roman writers such as Ammianus Marcellinus described them as terrifying mounted archers, but knew little about them. Any link to the Xiongnu of Mongolia is unproven.

What happened next, in a chain:

  • The Huns first beat the Alans on the steppe between the Volga and the Don, and many Alans joined them.
  • They then broke the Gothic kingdom of Ermanaric in what is now Ukraine.
  • In 376 tens of thousands of Goths came to the Danube and asked to enter the Roman Empire. They crossed, were badly treated, and rebelled.
  • In 378 they destroyed a Roman army and killed the emperor Valens at the Battle of Adrianople.

The Goths and others never left. Over the next century Germanic peoples settled across the western provinces, Rome was sacked by the Visigoths in 410, and the Western Roman Empire fell in 476. Historians call this the Migration Period.

The Huns themselves settled on the Hungarian plain and built the Hunnic Empire, which reached its height under Attila before breaking up after his death in 453.
sum: Around 370 the Huns, nomads from the steppe east of the Volga, crossed into Europe and attacked the peoples north of the Black Sea. It set off the great movement of peoples that ended Roman rule in the west.
